tests/unit/_fake_pymysql.py:70-80 does what the claim says. With no params it returns (lower_case_table_names,). With two params whose second is in server.kinds it returns (kinds[params[1]],). Otherwise it returns the first sorted stored routine whose lowercased name is among the params, or None. This matches src/sqllens/safety/relations.py. The probe `SELECT @@lower_case_table_names` at line 149 is called with no params, and the code reads mode[0]. The table lookup at lines 171-176 passes (relation.db or None, relation.name), so the second param is the relation name and the row is TABLE_TYPE. Edge case: a routine lookup with exactly two names whose second matches a kinds key would be treated as a table lookup. That is outside the claim, and the module docstring says tests must name their relations in kinds.

tests/unit/_fake_pymysql.py:70-80 _CatalogCursor.execute branches only on params: falsy -> (lower_case_table_names,); len==2 and params[1] in server.kinds -> (kinds[params[1]],); else first case-insensitive routine match or None. tests/integration/conftest.py:39-41 uses MYSQL_URL host db.invalid. RFC 2606 section 2 and RFC 6761 section 6.4 reserve .invalid, and require conforming resolvers to answer NXDOMAIN. The counterexamples I tried were a wildcard-DNS captive resolver and a hosts-file entry for db.invalid. A wildcard-DNS captive resolver is non-conforming. A hosts entry is a deliberate local override that someone would have to add on purpose for this exact name. The comment's wording, 'under a conforming resolver', excludes both. Nothing in the repo adds such an override. The rejection line in the item is about test_safety pragma rows and does not cover this claim.

first_sql_keyword (src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py:124-164) tokenizes with the mysql dialect and examines the first non-L_PAREN token. sqlglot tokens.py:154 maps '?' to TokenType.PLACEHOLDER, and the mysql dialect has no override of '?' or PLACEHOLDER.
